Description

Adrenaline and noradrenaline activate β2 adrenoceptors on nociceptors. Through Gs, adenylate cyclase and protein kinase A, they lower the threshold of the nerve endings and cause mechanical hyperalgesia. People with low COMT activity, who clear catecholamines more slowly, are more sensitive to pain, including OA pain.

References

  1. Khasar SG, McCarter G, Levine JD. Epinephrine produces a beta-adrenergic receptor-mediated mechanical hyperalgesia and in vitro sensitization of rat nociceptors. J Neurophysiol. 1999 Mar;81(3):1104-12. doi: 10.1152/jn.1999.81.3.1104. PMID: 10085337.
  2. Nackley AG, Tan KS, Fecho K, Flood P, Diatchenko L, Maixner W. Catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibition increases pain sensitivity through activation of both beta2- and beta3-adrenergic receptors. Pain. 2007 Apr;128(3):199-208. doi: 10.1016/j.pain.2006.09.022. PMID: 17084978.
